problem:
Consider the matrix differential equation 

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}]x(t)+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}].
$$

Which of the following vectors are solutions to this equation?

$$
{x}_{1}(t)=[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{2}(t)=[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}],\,{x}_{3}(t)=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]
$$
worked_solution:
Here, we need to substitute each vector into the given matrix differential equation and check if it results in a true statement.

For ${x}_{1}(t)$, we have

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}(t{e}^{t})^{′} \\ (t{e}^{t})^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} \\ (t+1){e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}t{e}^{t} \\ t{e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} \\ (t+1){e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & \ne [\begin{aligned}(t+1){e}^{t} \\ (t+1){e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Now, for ${x}_{2}(t)$, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}({e}^{t})^{′} \\ (0)^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}] & \ne [\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 2{e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Finally, for ${x}_{3}(t)$, we obtain 

$$
\begin{aligned}[\begin{aligned}(0)^{′} \\ ({e}^{t})^{′}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 \\ 1 & 0\end{aligned}][\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & =[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ 0\end{aligned}]+[\begin{aligned}{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] \\ [\begin{aligned}0 \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}] & \ne [\begin{aligned}2{e}^{t} \\ {e}^{t}\end{aligned}].\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, we conclude that the correct answer is "${x}_{1}(t)$ only".
